name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention (domain = inventory helper). No Ghidra address residue in the name. Accurately reflects purpose: search a char's inventory for a slot holding a given item id and return the slot index (-1 if none). Confirmed by all 5 callers using it exactly this way.
purpose: Search runtime_char[char_idx]'s inventory for the first slot holding item_id and return that slot index, or -1 if none.
logic_summary: slot_count = fd2_count_usable_inventory_slots(char_idx); if slot_count != 0, iterate slot_iter 0..slot_count-1, read each slot's item id via fd2_get_inventory_slot_item_id(char_idx, slot_iter), and return the first slot_iter whose id == item_id. Return -1 when count is 0 or no slot matches. fd2_get_inventory_slot_item_id returns a MOVZX zero-extended byte so the full-EAX compare is exactly a byte == item_id test.

params.name: char_idx
params.semantics: Index into the runtime_char array; identifies which character's inventory to search. Forwarded to fd2_count_usable_inventory_slots and fd2_get_inventory_slot_item_id. Callers pass 0..15 (e.g. fd2_any_char_has_item loop index).
params.reason: Precise, address-free, matches usage as the runtime_char array index.

params.name: item_id
params.semantics: The item id to find; compared (as a byte) against each slot's item id. Callers pass the searched key item id straight through (e.g. fd2_any_char_has_item forwards its own item_id; chapter handlers pass plot/promotion item ids).
params.reason: Precise, address-free, matches its role as the search key compared against each slot's item id byte.

returns.semantics: Slot index (0-based) of the first slot whose item id equals item_id; -1 if the usable slot count is 0 or no slot matches.

notes: Comment block at src/ui_menu/status.c lines 1159-1180 already concise, accurate, and ASCII (describes per-char usable-slot loop bound, per-slot id read, first-match return, -1 fallback, key-item use case, callers, and the MOVZX byte-compare nuance); kept as-is. Ghidra plate already consistent with src understanding; left unchanged. No reads/writes of globals (it only calls fd2_count_usable_inventory_slots and fd2_get_inventory_slot_item_id, which themselves touch data_fd2_battle_runtime_char_array_ptr). Loop bound is the usable-slot count, not a fixed 8 -- faithful and already documented; not a logic issue.
